video_title: Mahershala Ali Reveals Winning 2 Oscars Didn't Guarantee More Roles in Hollywood

quotes.speaker: Mahershala Ali
quotes.summary_phrase: Mahershala Ali on the limited impact of winning an Oscar on career opportunities
quotes.excerpt: There's a lot of great actors that don't have Oscars who are also looking for good material.
quotes.quote: There's a lot of great actors that don't have Oscars who are also looking for good material. It doesn't really mean anything. I'm not saying that's no disrespect to the Academy or the award at all, but what I'm actually saying is that Oscar or no Oscar, there's a lot of good actors out there. There's more good actors than there are good material. So it doesn't really mean anything. It's not even that all these people are competing for the same spots, it's just that there's only a handful of all the material made that check certain boxes, and then you got to be right for it. Just because the script is good, it doesn't mean that I'm right for it or that whoever wrote it is thinking about me of all people.

quotes.speaker: Mahershala Ali
quotes.summary_phrase: Mahershala Ali on the scarcity of roles written specifically for him
quotes.excerpt: The vast majority of projects that get greenlit, they're not roles for me.
quotes.quote: Who is centered in the vast majority of projects that get greenlit, they're not roles for me. You got to think that way. It don't matter if I got 17 Oscars. If someone is not writing something for you or greenlighting something with you in mind, you like everybody else waiting and looking and searching. Unless you're going to produce it and create it yourself, which is clearly always an option, but that's a five-year journey itself.

quotes.speaker: Mahershala Ali
quotes.summary_phrase: Mahershala Ali on the spam-like nature of post-Oscar career offers
quotes.excerpt: When you win an award, then suddenly, yeah, you can get a lot of phone calls.
quotes.quote: When you win an award, then suddenly, yeah, you can get a lot of phone calls, but it can be essentially, it can almost be like spam. Because you got to go through it and go, 'Ah, that doesn't fit. That's not a fit.' 15 pages in, 'Ah, not a fit.' I get where you're going with that, but that was really written for this and I don't feel, you know. So you can do it, and that's no disrespect to anybody sending me anything, but I'm just saying that it doesn't quite work that way.

quotes.speaker: Carmelo Anthony
quotes.summary_phrase: Carmelo Anthony and Mahershala Ali on the validation of winning an Oscar
quotes.excerpt: When black actors get Oscars, the preeminent notion around fans is like, 'All right, you are now validated.'

text_blocks.speaker: Carmelo Anthony
text_blocks.text: Is it different being a black actor though? Because I feel like once, especially, I remember when Denzel got his, when Halle got hers, Michael B. Jordan just got his. Like when black actors get Oscars, the preeminent notion around fans is like, 'All right, you are now officially on this list of people. You are now validated. You are in the Denzel class. You are in the class of A-list tier dudes.' And you're saying that it's kind of give and take. It's good but it's not.

text_blocks.speaker: Mahershala Ali
text_blocks.text: I just don't know what that means. I respectfully, meaning it's kind of just talk. You know, it's just it doesn't translate to anything real. It's just who's better, LeBron or Jordan? Who cares? They're great. There's no definitive answer. You know what I'm saying? So I think, and there's something to like, it's not the same world when Sydney Poitier won an Oscar as when Halle Berry or Viola Davis or, you know what I mean? It's different eras, different world.

quotes.speaker: Mahershala Ali
quotes.summary_phrase: Mahershala Ali on how political environments impact Hollywood hiring and diversity
quotes.excerpt: Because of things that have happened in our political environment and how those have trickled down.
quotes.quote: Because of things that have happened in our political environment and how those have trickled down into hiring practices, greenlighting practices, DEI being this bad word now, and all these other things that even stuff like that plays its part in companies feeling any type of healthy pressure to even sort of greenlight things that can even be perceived as being a diversity situation. And first of all, I don't even want to be associated with that type, not associated, but because diversity is a wonderful thing, but what I'm saying is you don't want to find yourself in a situation where, 'Oh, that's the diversity project.' You just want to do great material.

quotes.speaker: Mahershala Ali
quotes.summary_phrase: Mahershala Ali on being a black actor versus being an 'exotic other'
quotes.excerpt: As a black person, you're not thinking of yourself as this exotic other per se.
quotes.quote: As a black person, you're not thinking of yourself as this exotic other per se. You just are living your life. You wake up, you put your pants on like everybody else. You want to go, such an uphill battle, but you just want to be like, 'Yo, this is this is my offering. This is my story. This is my work,' opposed to, 'Man, are you, who are the best black actors?' And I remember hearing that conversation one time I was in grad school. I remember being so pissed off by it.

quotes.speaker: Mahershala Ali
quotes.summary_phrase: Mahershala Ali on the absurdity of comparing actors based on race
quotes.excerpt: I feel like it was Samuel Jackson on stage or something and someone goes, 'Oh, I love Samuel.'
quotes.quote: I remember, and I'm around a bunch of like actor actors, and they were, the Oscars were on. And there was like a TV in like our lobby. And there's three years there and there's all students filing in and out. But it was later on the day and there's not that many of us. There's only like 50 some kids in the whole program. But it was later in the evening, clearly and the Oscars are on and we're there six days a week. And I remember someone being like, I feel like it was Samuel Jackson on stage or something and someone goes, 'Oh, I love Samuel. He's he's so good.' And then someone else goes like, 'Yeah, but I like Morgan a little better.' And then someone was like, 'Yeah, well, Denzel is like that.' And suddenly there, it was like, and I was like so weirded out. It was like, why, why we got to be in this like, we got a different capacity because the color or something, you know? Or we just get into the best black actors, the best, I'm like, I'm an actor who happens to be black and I'll get down with anybody.

quotes.speaker: Mahershala Ali
quotes.summary_phrase: Mahershala Ali on how political pressures influence corporate greenlighting
quotes.excerpt: If certain companies are allowed to not feel a pressure to be reflective of the world.
quotes.quote: I think in some level it impacts what gets greenlit is what I'm saying. I'm not saying it, I don't know how much of an impact it has, but I just know that if certain companies are allowed to not feel a pressure to be reflective of the world we live in, they'll just keep centering who they see in their offices. And it ain't a bunch of us in those offices. And so that's all I'm really trying to say at the end of the day.
